summary: A farmer who takes a field to work for its owner must follow the local custom about cutting, pulling up and plowing. He and the owner share the straw and the vine branches just as they share the crop, and both give the poles.

chunks.en: If someone takes a field from his friend to farm,
chunks.explain: He works it and pays the owner with some of the crop.
chunks.st: With regard to one who receives a field from another
chunks.stMore: to cultivate, either as a tenant farmer, who, in exchange for the right to farm the land, gives a set amount of the produce to the owner, or as a sharecropper, who cultivates the land and receives a set proportion of the produce, the halakha is as follows:

chunks.en: where people usually cut the crop, he cuts it;
chunks.st: In a location where those cultivating the land were accustomed to cut the produce, this one must cut it as well.

chunks.en: to pull it up, he pulls it up;
chunks.st: In a location where they were accustomed to uproot the produce, not to cut it with a sickle or a scythe, this one must uproot it as well.

chunks.en: to plow after it, he plows.
chunks.st: If they were accustomed to plow the land after harvesting the produce, this one must plow as well.

chunks.en: Everything follows the custom of the place.
chunks.st: All farming of the land shall be conducted in accordance with regional custom.

chunks.en: Just as they split the grain,
chunks.st: Just as the halakha is that the owner of the field and the one cultivating it divide the produce,

chunks.en: so they split the straw and stubble.
chunks.st: so too the halakha is that they divide the stubble and the straw.

chunks.en: Just as they split the wine,
chunks.st: Just as the halakha is that the owner of the field and the one cultivating it divide the wine,

chunks.en: so they split the vine branches and the poles.
chunks.st: so too the halakha is that they divide the branches pruned from the vines and the poles.

chunks.en: And both of them give the poles.
chunks.explain: The poles hold up the grapevines.
chunks.st: And the two of them, i.e., the landowner and the one cultivating the field, both supply the poles.

summary: If a farmer took a watered field or a field of trees, and the spring dried up or the trees were cut down, he pays the full rent. But if he named the spring or trees in the deal, he may pay less.

chunks.en: If someone takes a field from his friend to farm,
chunks.st: In the case of one who receives a field from another to cultivate

chunks.he: וְהִיא בֵית הַשְּׁלָחִין אוֹ בֵית הָאִילָן,
chunks.en: and it is a watered field or a field of trees,
chunks.st: and it is an irrigated field or a field with trees,

chunks.en: and the spring dried up or the trees were cut down,
chunks.st: if the spring that irrigated the field dried up or the trees were cut down,

chunks.en: he does not take anything off his rent.
chunks.st: he does not subtract from the produce he owes the owner as part of his tenancy,
chunks.stMore: despite the fact that he presumably considered these factors when agreeing to cultivate the field.

chunks.en: But if he said to him,
chunks.st: But if the cultivator said to the landowner explicitly:

chunks.he: חֲכֹר לִי שְׂדֵה בֵית הַשְּׁלָחִין זֶה
chunks.en: "Rent me this watered field,"
chunks.st: Lease me this irrigated field,

chunks.en: or "this field of trees,"
chunks.st: or he said: Lease me this field with trees,

chunks.en: and the spring dried up or the trees were cut down,
chunks.st: and the spring dried up or the trees were cut down,

chunks.en: he takes it off his rent.
chunks.st: he may subtract from the produce he owes as part of his tenancy.

summary: A farmer who left the field he took unplanted must pay the owner what it could have grown, because the contract says so.

chunks.en: If someone takes a field from his friend and leaves it unplanted,
chunks.st: With regard to one who receives a field from another as a contractor and then lets it lie fallow and does not work the land at all,

chunks.en: they estimate it,
chunks.st: the court appraises it by evaluating

chunks.en: how much it could have grown,
chunks.st: how much it was able to produce if cultivated,

chunks.en: and he gives it to him,
chunks.st: and he gives his share of this amount to the owner.

chunks.en: because this is what he writes to him:
chunks.st: The reason is that this is what a cultivator writes to the owner in a standard contract:

chunks.en: "If I leave it unplanted and do not work it,
chunks.st: If I let the field lie fallow and do not cultivate it,

chunks.en: I will pay with the best."
chunks.st: I will pay with best-quality produce.

summary: A farmer who does not want to weed the field cannot say it is not the owner's business. The owner can say that after he leaves, the weeds will stay.

chunks.he: הַמְקַבֵּל שָׂדֶה מֵחֲבֵרוֹ וְלֹא רָצָה לְנַכֵּשׁ,
chunks.en: If someone took a field from his friend and did not want to weed it,
chunks.st: With regard to one who received a field from another to cultivate and did not want to weed it,

chunks.en: and he said to him, "What do you care,
chunks.st: and he then said to the owner: What do you care if I neglect the land? You will not suffer a loss

chunks.en: since I give you your rent?"
chunks.st: since I will give you the amount of produce I owe you for your granting me tenancy, regardless of the state of the field.

chunks.en: We do not listen to him,
chunks.st: Nevertheless, they do not listen to him.

chunks.en: because the owner can say to him,
chunks.st: The reason is because the owner of the land can say to him:

chunks.en: "Tomorrow you leave it,
chunks.st: Tomorrow you will depart from the field,

chunks.en: and it will grow weeds for me."
chunks.st: and it will grow weeds for me,
chunks.stMore: which will remain there and disrupt the yield of the field for years to come.

summary: A farmer must keep working a field that grows only a little, as long as there is enough for a pile. Rabbi Yehuda says it is enough if it grows as much as the seeds that were planted.

chunks.en: If someone took a field from his friend and it did not grow much,
chunks.st: With regard to one who receives a field from another to cultivate and it did not produce a sufficient crop to cover the expenses of its upkeep,

chunks.he: אִם יֶשׁ בָּהּ כְּדֵי לְהַעֲמִיד כְּרִי,
chunks.en: if it has enough to make a pile,
chunks.st: if it has enough produce to form a pile

chunks.en: he must keep working it.
chunks.st: he is obligated to take care of it and give the owner his share.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: "What size is a pile?
chunks.st: What fixed measure is a pile?
chunks.stMore: There is no inherent measure of produce that is considered significant, as it all depends on the size of the plot of land in question.

chunks.he: אֶלָּא אִם יֶשׁ בָּהּ כְּדֵי נְפִילָה:
chunks.en: Rather, if it has as much as the seeds that were planted."
chunks.st: Rather, the relevant issue is whether it has a crop equivalent to the measure of seeds for dropping in a field in order to sow it.

summary: If locusts or a bad wind ruined a farmer's crop, he pays less rent only if the whole area was hit. Rabbi Yehuda says if he pays rent in money, he never pays less.

chunks.en: If someone took a field from his friend
chunks.st: In the case of one who receives a field from another to cultivate

chunks.en: and locusts ate it or it was burnt by wind,
chunks.st: and grasshoppers consumed it or it was wind blasted,

chunks.en: if it is a plague of the whole area,
chunks.st: if it is a regional disaster which affected all the fields in the area,

chunks.en: he takes it off his rent.
chunks.st: the cultivator subtracts from the produce he owes as part of his tenancy.

chunks.en: If it is not a plague of the whole area,
chunks.st: If it is not a regional disaster,

chunks.en: he does not take it off his rent.
chunks.st: the cultivator does not subtract from the produce he owes as part of his tenancy.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: if he took it for money,
chunks.st: If the cultivator received it from the owner for a fixed sum of money,

chunks.en: either way
chunks.st: whether this way, i.e., there is a regional disaster, or whether that way, i.e., there was no regional disaster,

chunks.en: he does not take it off his rent.
chunks.st: he does not subtract the produce he owes as part of his tenancy.

summary: A farmer who pays rent in wheat gives wheat from the field itself, whether the crop is poor or very good.

chunks.en: If someone took a field from his friend
chunks.st: In the case of one who receives a field from another to cultivate

chunks.en: for ten kor of wheat a year,
chunks.st: in return for the payment of ten kor of wheat per year,

chunks.en: and it got sick, he gives him from it.
chunks.st: and its produce was blighted by a crop disease or the like, the cultivator gives the owner the ten kor of wheat from it but does not have to provide him with high quality wheat.

chunks.en: If its wheat was very good,
chunks.st: If the wheat stalks produced by the field were particularly good stalks of wheat,

chunks.en: he may not say to him,
chunks.st: the cultivator may not say to the owner:

chunks.en: "I will buy from the market,"
chunks.st: I will buy regular wheat from the market;

chunks.en: rather he gives him from it.
chunks.st: rather, he gives him from inside the field itself.

summary: A farmer who agreed to plant barley may not plant wheat, which is harder on the land. He may switch to an easier crop, but Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel forbids that too.

chunks.en: If someone takes a field from his friend to plant barley,
chunks.st: With regard to one who receives a field from another in order to plant it with barley,

chunks.en: he may not plant wheat.
chunks.st: he may not plant it with wheat, as wheat weakens the field more than barley does.

chunks.en: If wheat, he may plant barley;
chunks.st: But if he receives it in order to plant wheat, he may plant it with barley if he wishes,

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel forbids it.
chunks.st: but Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel forbids it.

chunks.en: Grain, he may not plant beans;
chunks.st: Similarly, if he receives it to plant it with grain he may not plant it with legumes, as they weaken the field more than grains do,

chunks.en: beans, he may plant grain;
chunks.st: but if he receives it in order to plant legumes he may plant it with grain,

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel forbids it.
chunks.st: but Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel forbids it.

summary: A farmer who takes a field for only a few years may not plant flax, which weakens the soil, or cut the sycamore branches. If he takes it for seven years, he may.

chunks.en: If someone takes a field from his friend for a few years,
chunks.st: One who receives a field from another to cultivate for a few years, i.e., fewer than seven,

chunks.en: he may not plant flax,
chunks.st: may not plant flax in it, as flax greatly weakens the soil,

chunks.en: and he has no right to the sycamore branches.
chunks.explain: They take many years to grow back.
chunks.st: and if a sycamore tree was growing in the field, he does not have rights to the beams fashioned from the branches of the sycamore
chunks.stMore: tree. Therefore, he may not cut down its branches for his own use, as it takes many years for new ones to grow.

chunks.en: If he took it for seven years,
chunks.st: If he received the field from him for seven years,

chunks.en: in the first year he may plant flax,
chunks.st: in the first year he may plant flax in it,

chunks.en: and he has a right to the sycamore branches.
chunks.st: and he does have rights to the beams fashioned from the branches of the sycamore tree.

summary: If a farmer rents a field for one shemittah cycle, the shemittah year counts. If he rents it for seven years, the shemittah year does not count, and he gets another year.

chunks.en: If someone took a field from his friend
chunks.st: In the case of one who receives a field from another to cultivate

chunks.en: for one shemittah cycle
chunks.explain: Seven years ending with shemittah, when we do not farm.
chunks.st: for one Sabbatical cycle of seven years culminating with the Sabbatical Year

chunks.en: for 700 zuz,
chunks.st: for seven hundred dinars,

chunks.en: the shemittah year is counted.
chunks.st: the Sabbatical Year is included in the tally, despite the fact that he is unable to work the land during that year.

chunks.en: If he took it for seven years
chunks.st: If he received it from him to cultivate for seven years

chunks.en: for 700 zuz,
chunks.st: for seven hundred dinars,

chunks.en: the shemittah year is not counted.
chunks.st: the Sabbatical Year is not included in the number,
chunks.stMore: and he may keep the field for an additional year to take the place of the Sabbatical Year, during which he could not work the land.

summary: A worker must be paid on time: a day worker by the end of that night, a night worker by the end of the next day, and other workers by when they finish.
stIntro: The tanna addresses a different issue, the halakha of the payment of workers.

chunks.en: A day worker can collect all that night.
chunks.explain: The employer has until morning to pay.
chunks.st: A day laborer collects his wages from his employer all night following his work shift.

chunks.en: A night worker can collect all the next day.
chunks.st: A night laborer collects his wages all the following day,

chunks.en: A worker by the hour
chunks.st: while an hourly laborer

chunks.en: collects all the night and all the day.
chunks.st: collects his wages all night and all day.

chunks.en: A worker for a week, for a month,
chunks.st: With regard to a weekly laborer, a monthly laborer,

chunks.en: for a year, or for seven years:
chunks.st: a yearly laborer, or a laborer for a Sabbatical cycle of seven years,

chunks.en: if he finished by day, he collects all that day;
chunks.st: if he left upon the completion of his work in the day, he collects his wages all day;

chunks.he: יָצָא בַלַּיְלָה, גּוֹבֶה כָל הַלַּיְלָה וְכָל הַיּוֹם:
chunks.en: if he finished at night, he collects all that night and the next day.
chunks.st: if he left at night, he collects his wages all night and all day.

summary: One must pay workers, and rent for animals and vessels, on time when they ask for it. The mishnah teaches when a worker can swear and take his pay, and what is different for a ger toshav.

chunks.en: Whether a person's pay,
chunks.st: Whether referring to a person’s wages that he receives

chunks.en: or rent for an animal,
chunks.st: or the renting of an animal

chunks.en: or rent for vessels,
chunks.st: or the renting of utensils,

chunks.en: all come under
chunks.st: are all subject to the prohibition of:

chunks.en: "On his day you shall give him his pay,"
chunks.st: “On the same day you shall give him his wages” (Deuteronomy 24:15),

chunks.en: and under
chunks.st: and are subject to the prohibition of:

chunks.en: "Do not keep a worker's pay
chunks.st: “The wages of a hired laborer shall not remain

chunks.en: with you until morning."
chunks.st: with you all night until the morning” (Leviticus 19:13).

chunks.en: When? When he asked for it.
chunks.st: When does he transgress these prohibitions? He transgresses them when the one owed the money claimed the payment from him.

chunks.en: If he did not ask for it, he does not break the mitzvah.
chunks.st: If he did not claim his payment from him the other does not transgress the prohibitions.

chunks.he: הִמְחָהוּ אֵצֶל חֶנְוָנִי אוֹ אֵצֶל שֻׁלְחָנִי,
chunks.en: If he sent him to be paid by a storekeeper or a money changer,
chunks.st: If the one who owes the money transferred his payment by leaving instructions with a storekeeper or with a money changer to pay him,

chunks.en: he does not break the mitzvah.
chunks.st: he does not transgress the prohibitions. The mishna discusses other related halakhot:

chunks.en: A worker, in his time, swears and takes his pay.
chunks.explain: If the employer says he already paid him.
chunks.st: If a hired laborer requests payment at the proper time and the employer claims he already paid him, the laborer takes an oath that he did not receive his wages and then takes the wages from the employer.

chunks.en: If his time passed, he does not swear and take.
chunks.st: If the time had passed, he does not take an oath and take the wages.

chunks.en: If there are witnesses that he asked for it,
chunks.st: If there are witnesses who testify that he claimed the money from him at the proper time,

chunks.en: he swears and takes.
chunks.st: he takes an oath and takes the money.

chunks.en: A ger toshav comes under
chunks.explain: A non-Jew who keeps the seven mitzvos of Bnei Noach.
chunks.st: One who hires a gentile who resides in Eretz Yisrael and observes the seven Noahide mitzvot [ger toshav]

chunks.en: "On his day you shall give him his pay,"
chunks.st: is subject to the prohibition of: “On the same day you shall give him his wages,”

chunks.en: but not under "Do not keep
chunks.st: but is not subject to the negative mitzva of:

chunks.en: a worker's pay with you until morning."
chunks.st: “The wages of a hired laborer shall not remain with you all night until the morning.”

summary: A lender may take a security only through beis din, and may not go into the borrower's house. He must give back what the poor man needs each day, and may not take from a widow or take things used to make food.

chunks.en: If someone lends money to his friend,
chunks.st: With regard to one who lends money to another and the debtor fails to repay it at the end of the term of the loan,

chunks.en: he may take a security only through beis din,
chunks.explain: A security is something kept until the loan is paid.
chunks.st: the creditor may take collateral from him to ensure payment only by means of an agent of the court, not of his own accord.

words.en: he should take a security from him

chunks.en: and he may not go into his house to take his security,
chunks.st: And he may not enter the debtor’s house to take his collateral,

chunks.en: as it says, "Stand outside."
chunks.st: as it is stated: “When you lend your neighbor any manner of loan, you shall not go into his house to take his collateral. You shall stand outside,
chunks.stMore: and the man to whom you lend shall bring forth the collateral to you outside” (Deuteronomy 24:10–11).

chunks.en: If he had two vessels,
chunks.st: If the debtor had two utensils of the same kind,

chunks.en: he takes one and leaves one.
chunks.st: the creditor takes one and leaves the other one in the debtor’s possession.

chunks.en: And he gives back the pillow at night
chunks.st: And in addition, the creditor must return a pillow at night, as the debtor requires it for sleeping,

chunks.en: and the plow by day.
chunks.st: and a plow, which is needed for his daytime work, by day.

chunks.en: And if he died,
chunks.st: If the debtor died,

chunks.en: he does not give it back to his heirs.
chunks.st: he is not required to return it to the debtor’s heirs.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: even to the borrower himself he gives it back
chunks.st: Even to the debtor himself he needs to return the collateral each day

chunks.en: only for thirty days,
chunks.st: only until thirty days have passed,

chunks.he: וּמִשְּׁלשִׁים יוֹם וּלְהַלָּן מוֹכְרָן בְּבֵית דִּין.
chunks.en: and after thirty days he sells them through beis din.
chunks.st: and from thirty days onward, the creditor can sell them in court, with the proceeds going toward payment of the debt.

chunks.he: אַלְמָנָה, בֵּין שֶׁהִיא עֲנִיָּה בֵּין שֶׁהִיא עֲשִׁירָה,
chunks.en: A widow, whether she is poor or rich,
chunks.st: With regard to a widow, whether she is poor or whether she is wealthy,

chunks.en: we may not take a security from her,
chunks.st: one may not take collateral from her,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "Do not take a widow's garment as a security."
chunks.st: “And you may not take the garment of a widow as collateral” (Deuteronomy 24:17).

chunks.en: One who takes millstones as a security
chunks.st: One who takes a millstone as collateral

words.en: the one who takes as security

chunks.en: breaks a "do not" mitzvah,
chunks.st: violates a prohibition,

chunks.en: and is punished for two vessels,
chunks.st: and he is liable for taking two vessels, i.e., both millstones in the pair,

chunks.en: as it says, "Do not take the lower or upper millstone as a security."
chunks.st: as it is stated: “He shall not take the lower or upper millstone as collateral” (Deuteronomy 24:6). The tanna adds:

chunks.en: And they did not say only the millstones,
chunks.st: Not only did the Sages say that it is prohibited to take the lower or upper millstone as collateral,

chunks.he: אֶלָּא כָל דָּבָר שֶׁעוֹשִׂין בּוֹ אֹכֶל נֶפֶשׁ,
chunks.en: but anything used to make food,
chunks.st: but they also said that one may not take anything that people use in the preparation of food [okhel nefesh],

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "For he is taking a life as a security."
chunks.explain: A person needs food to live.
chunks.st: “For he takes a man’s life [nefesh] as collateral” (Deuteronomy 24:6).
